claims.value: Side A: Höpfner estimates Ney still about 16,000 strong at Ankendorf after the first day’s action.

claims.value: The French bulletin has Ney withdraw according to his instructions; Höpfner identifies Bennigsen directing the attack with Sacken, Ostermann Tolstoy and Gallizin’s columns.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "he followed his instructions and took his corps to Ankendorf." English rendering (ours): "Bennigsen went ahead with some troops from Arendsdorf to Wolfsdorf and waited there for the columns."

claims.value: At Ankendorf, Höpfner describes a wood/lake anchoring Ney’s right and a marshy stream front toward the Passarge on his left.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "The right at Ankendorf rested on an occupied wood covered by the Queetz lake; the front ran obliquely along a stream with marshy meadow toward the Passarge"

citations.quote: Der rechte Flügel bei Ankendorf lehnte sich an einen besetzten Wald, der durch den Queetzer See gedeckt wurde; die Front lief schräg längs eines Baches mit sumpfigem Wiesengrunde nach der Passarge

claims.value: The Russian commander-in-chief attacked Ney’s positions, and renewed the attack at Deppen the following day.
claims.rationale: Ney’s limited forward movement at Ankendorf is a defensive counter-manoeuvre. English rendering (ours): "Meanwhile the Russian commander-in-chief with Grand Duke Constantine, the Russian Guard and three divisions attacked Ney’s positions at Altkirch, Amt-Guttstadt and Wolfsdorf"

citations.quote: Pendant ce temps, le général en chef russe, avec le grand-duc Constantin, la garde impériale russe et trois divisions, attaqua à la fois les positions du maréchal Ney sur Altkirch, Amt-Guttstadt et Wolfsdorf

claims.value: The French bulletin claims the enemy was repulsed at the initial positions and defeated at Deppen, while acknowledging Ney’s withdrawal.
claims.rationale: Retain against Bodart’s Russian winner; successful withdrawal and campaign contribution are distinct. English rendering (ours): "he was repulsed everywhere."
